hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 gets no input so a conv on edge 1->3 contributes nothing.
Edge 1->2 is dead when node 1 has no input, so upgrading it to conv gives no gain.
A conv on 1->3 is disconnected from the input when edge 0 is none.
A conv on 1->2 is disconnected when edge 0 is none, so its effect vanishes.
A skip on 1->3 carries nothing when node 1 is unreachable.
A skip on 1->2 carries nothing when node 1 is unreachable.
Replacing none on the direct input-output edge restores a path, a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
Adding a skip where there was none gives the biggest gain because it restores a gradient-friendly direct path.
Replacing none with a conv on the direct edge gains more than replacing an op that already gave a path.
Replacing none on edge 0 reconnects node 1 and enables all downstream edges, so the gain is much larger than replacing another op.
